newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: FOCUS - Amplats to develop "jewel in crown".
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Amplats to develop "jewel in crown".

text.p: The world's largest platinum producer, South Africa's Amplats, said on Tuesday it will start mining its "jewel in the crown" and also merge its existing four mines into one.

Amplats, Anglo American Platinum Corp of South Africa Ltd, announced plans to merge its four listed companies which at present constitute the group -- Rustenburg Platinum Holdings Ltd (Rusplat), Lebowa Platinum Mines Ltd (Leplat), Potgietersrust Platinums Ltd (PP Rust) and Amplats itself.
The merger, together with the development of a new mine at Boschkoppie and expansion of PP Rust's concentrator, would enhance Amplats position as world leader in platinum, the company said.
Amplats managing director Barry Davison said the development of Boschkoppie as a division of Rusplat, will see about 250,000 ounces of newly-mined platinum being produced.
"This is the jewel in the crown, that property (Boschkoppie)," Davison said.
The mine, on the rich Merensky Reef in South Africa's Rustenburg area, will reach full operation in 2002 and will be erected at a capital cost of 1.2 billion rand.
It will provide around 60 million tonnes of ore for milling at an estimated head grade for Platinum Group Metals (PGM) -- platinum, rhodium and palladium -- and gold of 6.1 grammes per tonne.
Amplats also said it was considering the merger of the four listed companies in the group.

"The proposed restructuring supports the Amplats group's strategy of moving its operations down the cost curve and increasing operational flexibility to take full advantage of market conditions by facilitating the optimal use of its combined asset base," the company said.

Davison said there was a gap in the market to increase its production as platinum demand is expected to increase by two percent per annum in the period to 2010 and Russian platinum supplies are seen dropping.
He said the expansion at Boschkoppie and PP Rust would see Amplats increase production from around 1.8 million ounces of platinum a year to 2.1 million ounces.
"By the time Boschkoppie comes on stream, the (supply) gap will be in the market place," Davison said.
Davison said Amplats expected the platinum business to remain a fundamentally good business up to 2010.
"We hopefully expect growth in volume demand of two percent per annum," he said.
"It certainly provides us with opportunities on the marketing side."
Amplats expects 1997 supply to total 4.963 million ounces against demand of 4.898 million, compared to supply of 4.850 million ounces in 1996 and demand of 4.770 million.
